guidance.when: When WISCONSIN is allowable and an asset is being valued.
guidance.procedure: Match § 815.18(3)(d) to listed personal, family, or household consumer goods, including firearms, with a whole-asset ceiling of $12,000 for one debtor or $24,000 for two equal joint debtors. Match § 815.18(3)(g) to a motor vehicle; when no used consumer-goods amount is supplied in this independent-pair task, its $4,000 vehicle amount plus unused (d) gives a $16,000 ceiling for one debtor or $32,000 for two equal joint debtors. Match § 815.20(1) only to an occupied homestead, capped at $75,000 for one debtor or $150,000 for two joint spouses. For every citation report the smaller of the whole asset value and that ceiling.
guidance.avoid_when: Do not put a motor vehicle under (3)(d). A firearm is consumer goods under (3)(d), not a depository account under (3)(k) or business property under (3)(b)(1) without the required account or business-use facts. Do not emit § 815.18(8), leave a half-interest as the result, or stop at one spouse's ceiling for jointly owned property where the statute permits both spouses' exemptions.
